title: Raise the tariff

predict.q: The tariff is doubled from 1 to 2 per unit. What happens to the government's tariff revenue?

options.s: It doubles, because each import now pays twice as much
options.fb: Each import pays twice as much, but imports fall from 40 to 20: revenue = tariff × imports, so 2 × 20 = 40, the same as 1 × 40.

options.s: It stays the same, because imports halve
options.fb: Imports fall from 40 to 20 while the tariff doubles: 2 × 20 = 40 = 1 × 40.

options.s: It falls to zero, because imports stop
options.fb: Imports stop only when the price reaches the no-trade price of 7, a tariff of 3. Slide to 3 to see it.

options.s: It falls, because domestic firms now supply the whole market
options.fb: Domestic firms supply more, 30 → 40, but consumption is 60, so 20 are still imported.

task: Move the **tariff** slider to 2 and watch the price, imports and the revenue rectangle and the deadweight-loss triangles.

target.do: Set the tariff to 2, then press Check.

takeaway: A higher tariff cuts imports, so revenue can stay flat or fall, while the deadweight loss grows faster than the tariff. At a tariff of 3 imports stop entirely.
